title: Participle Clauses
completion_message: ¡Soberbio! Has dominado las Participle Clauses. Estas estructuras son el sello distintivo de la escritura formal, los informes ejecutivos y la comunicación corporativa de más alto nivel.

parts.visual:
En nivel C1, en lugar de usar conectores básicos (because, if, when), usamos Participle Clauses para escribir de forma más formal y concisa. 
1. Para expresar RAZÓN (en lugar de Because/Since): 
Normal: Because she needed more time, she asked for an extension. 
C1 (Present Participle): NEEDING more time, she asked for an extension. 
Normal: Because I was exhausted, I went to sleep. 
C1 (Past Participle): EXHAUSTED, I went to sleep.
parts.audio: At the C1 level, instead of using basic connectors like because, if, or when, we use Participle Clauses to write more formally and concisely. First, to express a reason, instead of 'because'. Normal sentence: Because she needed more time, she asked for an extension. C1 version: Needing more time, she asked for an extension. Another example: Because I was exhausted, I went to sleep. C1 version: Exhausted, I went to sleep.

parts.visual:
2. Para acciones secuenciales (una después de otra): 
Normal: After I finished the report, I sent it. 
C1 (Perfect Participle): HAVING FINISHED the report, I sent it. 

3. Cláusula Pasiva (Having been + participio): 
Normal: After it was approved by the board, the project started. 
C1: HAVING BEEN APPROVED by the board, the project started. 
*Ojo: El sujeto de ambas acciones debe ser el mismo.
parts.audio: Second, for sequential actions, one after another. Normal sentence: After I finished the report, I sent it. C1 version using a Perfect Participle: Having finished the report, I sent it. Third, Passive Clauses. Normal: After it was approved by the board, the project started. C1 version: Having been approved by the board, the project started. Important note: The subject of both clauses must be exactly the same for this to work.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige la cláusula de participio correcta (forma -ing, past participle o having + participle).

questions.question: ____ the email, he realized he had made a mistake. (Habiendo enviado / Después de enviar).
questions.explanation: Acción completada antes que otra: Having + past participle (Having sent).

questions.question: ____ by the lack of progress, the CEO cancelled the project. (Frustrado / Como estaba frustrado).
questions.explanation: Estado/Razón pasiva: Frustrated (Como estaba frustrado, el CEO...).

questions.question: ____ for a multinational company, she travels a lot. (Trabajando / Como trabaja).
questions.explanation: Acción continua/Razón activa: Working (Debido a que trabaja...).

questions.question: ____ all her money, she couldn't afford to buy the ticket. (Habiendo gastado).
questions.explanation: Acción pasada que causa un resultado: Having spent.

questions.question: ____ by the committee, the proposal was implemented immediately. (Habiendo sido aprobada).
questions.explanation: Pasiva perfecta (After it was approved): Having been approved.

questions.question: ____ no other option, we had to lay off 50 employees. (Teniendo / Al no tener otra opción).
questions.explanation: Razón presente activa: Having no other option (= Because we had no other option).

questions.question: ____ in 1995, the company has grown significantly. (Fundada / Al haber sido fundada).
questions.explanation: Participio pasado pasivo: Founded (= Because it was founded in 1995).

questions.question: Not ____ what to do, I asked my manager for advice. (No sabiendo).
questions.explanation: Negación en participio (Razón activa): Not knowing (= Because I didn't know).

questions.question: ____ to impress the client, he prepared an excellent presentation. (Esperando/Con la esperanza de).
questions.explanation: Razón activa: Hoping (= Because he hoped).

questions.question: ____ five languages, she is an asset to the international team. (Hablando / Como habla).
questions.explanation: Característica/Razón activa: Speaking (= Because she speaks).

questions.question: Not ____ invited to the meeting, John stayed at his desk. (Al no haber sido invitado).
questions.explanation: Negación perfecta pasiva: Not having been invited (= Because he had not been invited).

questions.question: ____ the document carefully, she signed on the last page. (Habiendo leído).
questions.explanation: Secuencia temporal (primero lee, luego firma): Having read.

questions.question: ____ out of printer ink, I couldn't print the contract. (Habiéndome quedado sin).
questions.explanation: Having run out of (= Because I had run out of).

questions.question: ____ down the street, I ran into my old boss. (Caminando / Mientras caminaba).
questions.explanation: Acción simultánea (mientras): Walking (= While I was walking).

questions.question: ____ in Japan, the cars are of excellent quality. (Fabricados / Al estar fabricados).
questions.explanation: Participio pasado pasivo: Manufactured (= Because they are manufactured).

questions.question: ____ to answer the journalist's questions, the CEO ended the press conference. (Rehusándose / Al negarse).
questions.explanation: Razón activa: Refusing (= Because he refused).

questions.question: ____ the warning signs, they invested heavily in the failing company. (Ignorando).
questions.explanation: Acción activa: Ignoring (= Because/While they ignored).

questions.question: ____ by a famous architect, the new headquarters cost $500 million. (Diseñada).
questions.explanation: Pasiva: Designed (= Because/As it was designed).

questions.question: Never ____ to Paris before, she was very excited about the business trip. (No habiendo estado nunca).
questions.explanation: Negación + Perfect Participle: Never having been (= Because she had never been).

questions.question: ____ the truth, I wouldn't have signed the agreement. (Conociendo / Si hubiera sabido).
questions.explanation: En este caso 'Knowing the truth' equivale a una condición (If I had known the truth). 'Knowing' es correcto.

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la palabra o participio correcto para formar la cláusula (Having, Working, Exhausted, etc).

questions.question: ____ (work) for Apple, he knows a lot about tech. (Trabajando / Al trabajar)
questions.explanation: Working.

questions.question: ____ (finish) the report, I went home. (Habiendo terminado)
questions.explanation: Having finished.

questions.question: ____ (exhaust), I fell asleep during the meeting. (Exhausto / Como estaba exhausto)
questions.explanation: Exhausted.

questions.question: Not ____ (know) what to do, I asked for help. (No sabiendo)
questions.explanation: knowing.

questions.question: ____ (found) in 1990, the company is very old. (Fundada / Al ser fundada)
questions.explanation: Founded.

questions.question: ____ been approved, the project started. (Habiendo sido aprobado - falta la primera palabra)
questions.explanation: Having.

questions.question: ____ (need) more money, we went to the bank. (Necesitando)
questions.explanation: Needing.

questions.question: ____ (spend) all the budget, we had to stop. (Habiendo gastado)
questions.explanation: Having spent.

questions.question: ____ (design) by experts, the app is flawless. (Diseñada)
questions.explanation: Designed.

questions.question: ____ no other option, I resigned. (Teniendo - palabra con H)
questions.explanation: Having.

pairs.target: Trabajando para el gobierno (como trabajo para...)
Exhausto por el trabajo (como estaba exhausto...)
